name: LT3080EST#TRPBF
title: LT3080: 1.1A adjustable low-dropout regulator set by a single resistor, parallelable
summary: The LT3080 is a 1.1A linear regulator built as a precision 10µA current source driving a unity-gain power follower: one resistor from SET to ground sets the output anywhere from 0V to 36V, and several parts can be paralleled for more current or to spread heat. The pass-transistor collector (IN) has its own pin, so with a separate higher VCONTROL supply IN needs only about 350mV of headroom; tied together (and always in the SOT-223) dropout is about 1.35V. It has no ground pin, needs 0.5mA to 1mA of minimum load, is stable with 2.2µF of ceramic output capacitance, and has current limit with foldback and thermal shutdown. Packages: 8-lead MSOP and 3mm × 3mm DFN with exposed pad, 5-lead DD-Pak and TO-220, 3-lead SOT-223; E and I grades from –40°C to 125°C; automotive #W versions in SOT-223, and AEC-Q100 qualified for automotive applications.

notes: E and I in the name are the temperature grade; DD, MS8E, Q, T and ST are the package; #PBF marks a lead-free finish, #TR and #TRPBF tape and reel. The grade is shown on a label on the shipping container, not on the part.
Some packages also come on 500-piece reels with the suffix #TRMPBF. The TO-220 has no tape-and-reel option.
The #W versions (SOT-223 only) are made under controlled manufacturing for automotive quality and reliability requirements; only these are offered for automotive applications.
In the SOT-223, IN and VCONTROL are joined inside the package; the 350mV VIN dropout figure does not apply to it.

circuits.title: Variable output voltage 1.1A supply
circuits.description: The simplest LT3080 regulator in three-terminal mode: IN and VCONTROL share the 1.2V to 36V input, which is bypassed by 1µF, and one resistor from SET to ground sets the output at RSET × 10µA. A 2.2µF capacitor on the output keeps the loop stable.

circuits.title: Basic adjustable regulator
circuits.description: The regulator with its two supplies kept apart: one source feeds IN (the pass-transistor collector) and a second feeds VCONTROL. RSET from SET to ground sets the output; CSET across RSET lowers noise and improves transient response, and COUT on the output gives stability.

circuits.title: Parallel devices
circuits.description: Two LT3080s share a 3.3V, 2A load. Their IN and VCONTROL pins share the 4.8V to 28V input (1µF bypass), their SET pins are joined to one 165k resistor to ground, and each output reaches the common 3.3V node through a 10mΩ ballast resistor that evens out the two currents. 10µF on the shared output.

circuits.title: Connections for best load regulation
circuits.description: How to wire the regulator to a distant load. The three RP resistors are the resistance of the wiring. RSET returns through its own wire to the negative end of the load rather than to the regulator's ground, so the drop in the ground return does not add to the output error; the drop in the positive wire still does.

parts.note: parasitic wiring resistance, OUT to load
parasitic wiring resistance, RSET to load return
parasitic wiring resistance, load return to ground

circuits.title: Reducing power dissipation using a series resistor
circuits.description: VCONTROL takes the full input while IN is fed through RS. The drop across RS lowers the IN-to-OUT voltage and so moves part of the heat out of the package into the resistor. C1 bypasses the input, C2 is the output capacitor and RSET sets the output.

circuits.title: Reducing power dissipation using a parallel resistor
circuits.description: RP runs from the input straight to the output beside the regulator, carrying part of the load current so less of it, and less heat, passes through the LT3080. It suits a steady input and a load that changes little. C1 bypasses the input, C2 is the output capacitor and RSET sets the output.

circuits.title: Higher output current
circuits.description: An external MJ4502 PNP adds current: 3.3V at 5A from 6V. IN is fed from the input through 50Ω and drives the PNP's base, and the PNP's collector joins the output. VCONTROL is on the 6V input, 332k on SET gives 3.3V, and 100µF plus 1µF bypass the input while 4.7µF and 100µF sit on the output.

circuits.title: Adding shutdown
circuits.description: The ON/OFF line drives the gates of two VN2222LL MOSFETs. With Q1 on, SET is shorted to ground and the output goes to zero; Q2 pulls the output to ground so it reaches zero even with no load attached. A 1N4148 runs from OUT to SET. R1 sets the output voltage in normal running.
notes: Q2 makes the output reach zero when no load is connected.

circuits.title: Current source
circuits.description: An adjustable 0A to 1A current source from a 10V supply. The output passes through a 1Ω sense resistor, and the 100k variable resistor runs from SET to the far side of that resistor; the regulator holds 10µA × R across the 1Ω, so the 100k setting chooses the output current. 1µF bypasses the input and 4.7µF sits on the output.

circuits.title: Low dropout voltage LED driver
circuits.description: A 100mA LED driver. The LED sits between the supply and IN, and R2 (2.49Ω) from OUT to ground sets the current: R1 (24.9k) puts 249mV on SET, which the output copies across R2. VCONTROL is on the supply, bypassed by C1.

circuits.title: Using a lower value SET resistor
circuits.description: The output is set with a 10k potentiometer instead of a large resistor. R2 (499Ω) from the output draws 1mA into the node below R1 (49.9k), so the potentiometer carries 1mA plus the 10µA SET current and the output spans 0.5V to 10V from a 12V input. C1 (1µF) bypasses the input and COUT (4.7µF) the output.
notes: VOUT = 0.5V + (1mA + 10µA) • RSET

circuits.title: Coincident tracking
circuits.description: Three LT3080s on one 7V to 28V input give 2.5V (1A), 3.3V and 5V that rise and fall together. U1 sets 2.5V with 249k to ground; U2's SET resistor (80.6k) returns to U1's output instead of ground, adding 0.8V; U3's (169k) returns to U2's output, adding 1.7V. Each output has 4.7µF; C1 (1.5µF) bypasses the input.

circuits.title: Adding soft-start
circuits.description: A 3.3V, 1A regulator from 4.8V to 28V whose output ramps up slowly. C2 (0.01µF) from SET to ground has to charge through the 10µA SET current, so the output climbs at the rate of the SET voltage; R1 (332k) sets the final 3.3V. A 1N4148 runs from SET to the input. C1 (1µF) bypasses the input and COUT (4.7µF) the output.

circuits.title: Lab supply
circuits.description: A bench supply with both current and voltage adjustable, from 12V to 18V. U1 is a current source: its output runs through 1Ω, and the 100k variable resistor from its SET to the far side of the 1Ω sets the limit from 0A to 1A. That current-limited node (15µF) feeds IN and VCONTROL of U2, whose 1MEG variable SET resistor sets the output from 0V to 10V. 15µF bypasses the input; 4.7µF and 100µF are on the output.

circuits.title: High voltage regulator
circuits.description: A 20V, 1A output from a 50V input. A BUZ11 N-channel MOSFET drops most of the input ahead of the LT3080: its gate is held by the 6.1V Zener above the output, fed from the input through 10k, so the IN/VCONTROL node sits a fixed amount above VOUT whatever the input. A 1N4148 runs from that node to the gate. RSET (2MEG) gives 20V. 10µF bypasses the input, 15µF the intermediate node and 4.7µF the output.
notes: VOUT = 20V
VOUT = 10µA • RSET

circuits.title: Ramp generator
circuits.description: The 10µA SET current charges a 1µF capacitor on SET, so the output ramps up linearly from a 5V supply. A square-wave input drives two VN2222LL MOSFETs: one discharges the SET capacitor, the other pulls the output down, with the 1N4148 from OUT to SET. 1µF bypasses the input and 4.7µF the output.

circuits.title: Reference buffer
circuits.description: An LT1019 reference drives SET directly, and the LT3080 follows it as a unity-gain power buffer, so the output carries the reference's accuracy instead of the SET-current and resistor tolerances. C1 (1µF) on SET and C2 (4.7µF) on the output. The load must draw at least 0.5mA.
notes: Minimum load 0.5mA.

circuits.title: Ground clamp
circuits.description: An outside signal VEXT drives the output node through 20Ω. The LT3080, with 5k from SET to ground, sources current to keep that node from going below its set level near ground, so a sine wave at VEXT comes out at VOUT with its lower half clipped off. A 1N4148 runs from OUT to SET. 1µF bypasses the input and 4.7µF sits on the output.

circuits.title: Boosting fixed output regulators
circuits.description: An LT3080 adds current to an LT1963-3.3 fixed regulator for 3.3V at 2.6A from 5V. Each output reaches the load through 20mΩ. The LT3080's SET is taken from a 42Ω/33k divider off the LT1963 output, about 4mV below it, so the LT3080 stays off at no load and supplies current only as the load grows. More than one LT3080 can be added. 10µF on the input, 47µF on the output.
notes: The 4mV drop keeps the LT3080 off with no load.
Several LT3080s can be used.

circuits.title: Low voltage, high current adjustable high efficiency regulator
circuits.description: An LTC3414 synchronous buck converter pre-regulates the IN supply of four paralleled LT3080s, giving 0V to 4V at 4A from 2.7V to 5.5V. The VCONTROL pins take the raw input. A 2N3906 PNP, emitter on the buck output and base through 10k to the final output, pulls the buck's feedback node so the buck output stays one VBE (about 0.6V) above the LT3080 output, keeping their dissipation low. The four SET pins share one 100k potentiometer; each output joins the 100µF output node through 20mΩ. The output can reach no closer than 1.5V below the input.

circuits.title: Adjustable high efficiency regulator
circuits.description: An LT3493 buck converter pre-regulates IN and VCONTROL of the LT3080 for 0V to 10V at 1A from 4.5V to 25V. A TP0610L P-channel MOSFET, source on the buck output and gate through 10k to the final output, pulls the buck's feedback node so the buck output tracks about one P-channel threshold (≈1.4V) above the LT3080 output. The 1MEG potentiometer on SET sets the output. Around the LT3493: CMDSH-4E and 0.1µF boost, MBRM140 catch diode, 10µH and 68µF output filter, 200k/10k feedback, 100k and 0.1µF on SHDN, 10µF and 1µF on the input. The output can reach no closer than 2V below the input.
notes: The LT3080 input-to-output difference is about 1.4V, set by the TP0610L threshold.
The maximum output voltage is 2V below the input voltage.

circuits.title: 2 terminal current source
circuits.description: A current source with only two terminals. IN and VCONTROL are the positive terminal; the 100k resistor from SET and the sense resistor R1 from OUT meet at the negative terminal. SET sits 1V (10µA × 100k) from that node and OUT follows it, so 1V lies across R1 and the current is 1V/R1. CCOMP from the positive terminal to OUT keeps it stable: 10µF for R1 ≤ 10Ω, 2.2µF for R1 ≥ 10Ω.
notes: IOUT = 1V / R1

circuits.title: Paralleling regulators
circuits.description: Two LT3080s share a 3.3V, 2A load. Their IN and VCONTROL pins share the 4.8V to 28V input (1µF bypass), their SET pins are joined to one 165k resistor to ground, and each output reaches the common 3.3V node through a 20mΩ ballast resistor. 10µF on the shared output.

operation.text: A 10µA current source with a near-zero temperature coefficient feeds the non-inverting input of a power operational amplifier wired as a unity-gain follower; the output copies the SET voltage at low impedance. One resistor from SET to ground sets the output, and a zero-ohm resistor gives zero volts. Because the reference is a true current source rather than a bootstrapped voltage, the loop gain and bandwidth do not change with output voltage or with a capacitor on SET, and regulation is a fixed number of millivolts rather than a percentage of the output.

The collector of the pass transistor (IN) is a separate pin from the control supply (VCONTROL). Tied together, the part is a three-terminal regulator with about 1.35V of dropout. With VCONTROL on a higher rail and IN on a lower one, IN needs only about 350mV, which cuts dissipation: for example 2.5V in to 1.8V out, or 1.8V in to 1.2V out, at 1.1A. A resistor in series with IN moves more of the heat onto the board.

The SET voltage is the SET current times RSET and becomes the error amplifier's reference; there is no lower limit on the output. At least 1mA of load is needed at any output voltage. To regulate at a true 0V, that 1mA must flow to a negative supply.

SET is a high-impedance node fed by only 10µA, so 10nA of leakage into or out of it makes a 0.1% error in the reference. Good insulation (Teflon, Kel-F), removal of flux and residue, and a surface coating in humid conditions help. A guard ring round SET and its parts, tied to OUT and run on both sides of the board, cuts board leakage; how much bulk leakage it removes depends on the ring's width.

Signals coupling into SET can cause erratic behaviour, most of all with the minimum output capacitance at full load; 10pF to 20pF from SET to ground cures it. A capacitor of up to 1µF across RSET improves transient response and lowers noise, but start-up time then grows with the RSET × CSET time constant.

The output needs a capacitor for stability: at least 2.2µF with ESR of 0.5Ω or less. Ceramic, tantalum and low-ESR electrolytic types all work, and ceramics need no added ESR. More capacitance lowers peak deviation on large load steps. Bypass capacitors at the loads count toward the total.

Z5U and Y5V parts lose much of their value with DC bias and temperature: a 16V 10µF Y5V on a 5V output can be as little as 1µF to 2µF in use. X5R and X7R are more stable and better suited to the output; X7R holds up better over temperature while X5R is cheaper and comes in larger values. Even these lose capacitance under DC bias, less so in larger cases, so the value at the working voltage should be checked. Some ceramics are piezoelectric and turn vibration or thermal shock into voltage.

LT3080s can be paralleled for more current: SET pins joined, IN pins joined, in three-terminal mode or with separate supplies, and the outputs connected through a small ballast resistance, which can be a short length of board trace (Table 1). The worst-case SET-to-OUT offset of ±2mV allows very small ballast: 10mΩ per device shares the current to better than 80% at full output. The resulting 5mΩ adds about 10mV of drop at 2A, about 1% at a 1V output. More devices can be added and spread over the board; input resistors spread the heat further when the input-to-output difference is large.

Two DFN parts about 1.5in apart on a vertical 1oz four-layer board: at about 0.7V input-to-output and 1A each (700mW each, 2A total) they rose about 28°C above ambient, within ±1°C of each other, and the board was back at ambient within about 0.5in. At 1.7V across each (1.7W each) they reached about 90°C, about 65°C above a 25°C ambient, matched within 2°C, with the board at about 40°C 0.75in away. 3m/s of air across them lowers the device temperature by about 20°C. In hotter surroundings the junction must still be kept below 125°C.

The reference current has about 3.2pA/√Hz of noise (1nARMS from 10Hz to 100kHz); multiplied by RSET it becomes a voltage, which adds as an RMS sum to the resistor's own √(4kTR) noise. A capacitor across RSET lowers this part, at the cost of slower start-up. The error amplifier adds about 125nV/√Hz (40µVRMS over 10Hz to 100kHz). Because SET to OUT is unity gain, none of this is amplified at higher output voltages. SET can also be driven from a precision voltage reference to remove the SET-current and resistor tolerances.

Safe-operating-area protection pulls the current limit down as the input-to-output difference grows, keeping dissipation safe; some output current is available at every input-to-output voltage up to breakdown. At power-up the output follows the rising input, so the part can start into heavy loads. With a high input, a low output and a heavy load (for example right after a short is removed) the load line can cross the current-limit curve twice, giving two stable operating points; the input may then have to be taken to zero and brought back up for the output to recover.

The part has no ground pin; all quiescent and drive current goes to the load, so true remote sensing is not possible. Load regulation is specified with Kelvin sensing at the package. Returning the bottom of RSET to the negative side of the load gives a true Kelvin connection on that side; overall regulation is then the LT3080's own figure plus the positive-lead resistance times the output current, so that lead should be short and heavy.

Internal power and thermal limiting protect the part under overload, but in normal running the maximum junction temperature must be respected, counting every path from junction to ambient and any nearby heat sources. Surface-mount parts are cooled by board copper, plated through-holes or surface-mount heat sinks. θJC is measured from the junction to the bottom of the case under the die, the lowest-resistance path. On the TO-220, thermal compound is strongly advised at the heat-sink joint; an insulating spacer may be used if its thermal resistance is allowed for. The tab or exposed pad is electrically OUT. The copper-area tables were measured in still air on a two-sided 1/16in FR-4 board with 1oz copper.

Output 0.9V, VCONTROL 3.3V ±10% (3.630V maximum), IN 1.5V ±5% (1.575V maximum), 1mA to 1A, 50°C ambient, DFN on a 2500mm² board with 500mm² of top copper: ICONTROL = 1A/60 = 17mA; PDRIVE = (3.630V – 0.9V)(17mA) = 46mW; POUTPUT = (1.575V – 0.9V)(1A) = 675mW; total 721mW. TJ = 50°C + 721mW × 64°C/W = 96°C, below the maximum.

operation.topic: Reducing dissipation with a series resistor
operation.text: With VIN = VCONTROL = 5V, VOUT = 3.3V and 1A, the LT3080 dissipates (5V – 3.3V)(1A/60) + (5V – 3.3V)(1A) = 1.73W. Leaving 0.5V across the pass transistor needs RS = 1.2Ω; the LT3080 then dissipates (5V – 3.3V)(1A/60) + 0.5V × 1A = 0.53W, about 30% of before, and RS takes 1.2W, so its power rating must suit.

operation.topic: Reducing dissipation with a parallel resistor
operation.text: A resistor from input to output carries part of the load. It suits a fairly constant input and small load changes, and it raises the available current at the cost of a higher minimum load. Example: VIN = VCONTROL = 5V (5.5V maximum), VOUT = 3.3V (3.2V minimum), load 0.7A to 1A, RP carrying no more than 90% of 0.7A = 630mA: RP = 3.65Ω, 3.6Ω as a 5% value. Total dissipation at most is (5.5V – 3.2V) × 1A = 2.3W, but the LT3080 supplies only 0.36A and dissipates (5.5V – 3.2V) × 0.36A = 0.83W, while RP dissipates 1.47W. The load can then grow by 0.64A, to 1.64A, with the LT3080 still in its normal range.
Short-circuit protection, safe-operating-area protection with current-limit foldback, and thermal shutdown are built in. The output can be shorted indefinitely.
